GRADE Certainty Assessment

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source

GRADE certainty was assessed per the GRADE Handbook (Schünemann et al.), adapted for Bayesian meta-analyses of observational studies. Starting certainty for all outcomes is LOW (observational evidence).

Summary

CMV Reactivation

Show code 
tibble::tribble(
  ~Domain, ~C1, ~C2,
  "Study design", "All retrospective; start LOW", "All retrospective; start LOW",
  "Risk of bias", "0 (ascertainment bias noted)", "0 (direction uncertain)",
  "Inconsistency", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 69%)", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 67%)",
  "Indirectness", "0", "0",
  "Imprecision", "0 (CrI excludes null)", "\u22121 (CrI fragile; crosses null in M2 and sensitivity)",
  "Upgrade", "+1 (steroid-independence confirmed)", "+1 (mechanistic coherence with C1 reversal)",
  "Net", "0", "\u22121",
  "CERTAINTY", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW"
) |>
  kable() |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE)
ImportantCMV: The Reversal Is More Informative Than Either Estimate

Neither the C1 CMV estimate (OR 1.41, LOW certainty) nor the C2 estimate (OR 0.77, VERY LOW certainty) alone provides high confidence. However, the contrast between them — PTCy harmful vs CNI+MTX/MMF but protective vs ATG — provides moderate-certainty evidence that CMV risk is ordered by T-cell depletion depth. This cross-comparison finding has higher certainty than either component.

Narrative Summary

Across both comparisons, certainty does not exceed LOW — a predictable consequence of an almost entirely observational evidence base.

Cross-comparison coherence is the strongest methodological asset. OS and aGVHD show consistent effects across two fundamentally different comparators, reducing the probability that findings are artefacts of comparator-specific confounding. The mediation pattern also replicates (OS: partial; NRM: substantial/complete).

The CMV direction reversal provides moderate-certainty mechanistic evidence. Any C2 value below ~1.0 confirms a qualitative direction shift, making this finding robust to the specific C2 point estimate.

Infection outcomes remain the principal evidence gap. BSI and IFI carry VERY LOW certainty in both comparisons. Dedicated prospective studies with standardised endpoint definitions are needed.

## CMV: The Reversal Is More Informative Than Either Estimate
Neither the C1 CMV estimate (OR 1.41, LOW certainty) nor the C2 estimate (OR 0.77, VERY LOW certainty) alone provides high confidence. However, the *contrast* between them — PTCy harmful vs CNI+MTX/MMF but protective vs ATG — provides **moderate-certainty evidence** that CMV risk is ordered by T-cell depletion depth. This cross-comparison finding has higher certainty than either component.
:::

## Narrative Summary {#sec-grade-narrative}

Across both comparisons, certainty does not exceed LOW — a predictable consequence of an almost entirely observational evidence base.

**Cross-comparison coherence** is the strongest methodological asset. OS and aGVHD show consistent effects across two fundamentally different comparators, reducing the probability that findings are artefacts of comparator-specific confounding. The mediation pattern also replicates (OS: partial; NRM: substantial/complete).

**The CMV direction reversal** provides moderate-certainty mechanistic evidence. Any C2 value below ~1.0 confirms a qualitative direction shift, making this finding robust to the specific C2 point estimate.

**Infection outcomes remain the principal evidence gap.** BSI and IFI carry VERY LOW certainty in both comparisons. Dedicated prospective studies with standardised endpoint definitions are needed.
